title: A unique geometric point at a prime has purely inseparable residue extension
statement: Let $A\to C$ be an integral map, $\Omega$ an algebraically closed field, and $\phi:A\to\Omega$. Let $t:C\to\Omega$ extend $\phi$. Suppose every other extension $t'$ with kernel equal to $\ker t$ equals $t$. Then the induced residue-field map $\kappa(\ker\phi)\to\kappa(\ker t)$ [def-weil-residue-field] is purely inseparable. The same holds with primes explicitly identified with those kernels.

source.place: Tags 00UJ and 00UL (etale local splitting), with geometric-point refinement proved in lean/WeilConjectures/Mathlib/RingTheory/Etale/GeometricPoint.lean; field-embedding and residue-field arguments are given in that source module.

proof.text: Use phi to embed its residue field into Omega. Integrality makes the extension to the residue field of ker t algebraic. Each embedding of that extension in Omega gives a point of C extending phi with kernel ker t. The hypothesis equates these points; equality on C determines equality on its residue field by the fraction-field universal property. Thus there is at most one embedding in Omega. The algebraic embedding equivalence with the algebraic closure and Mathlib isPurelyInseparable_iff_subsingleton_emb imply pure inseparability. Substituting the explicit equalities of primes gives the primed form. This is the complete existing proof in GeometricPoint.lean:233-273; the pinned sorry map records no reachable holes.

lemma isPurelyInseparable_of_forall_eq' [Algebra.IsIntegral A B] (t : PointsOver φ B)
    (h : ∀ t' : PointsOver φ B, RingHom.ker t'.1 = RingHom.ker t.1 → t' = t)
    (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] (hp : RingHom.ker φ = p) (q : Ideal B) [q.IsPrime]
    (hq : RingHom.ker t.1 = q) (hpq : p = q.comap (algebraMap A B)) :
    (Ideal.ResidueField.map p q (algebraMap A B) hpq).IsPurelyInseparable
